sections.body:
A toy is an object we play with. We use it to have fun, to learn and to imagine.

A toy can be anything you can hold and play with. It might be made of wood, plastic, cloth or metal. A **block**, a **ball**, a **doll** and a **puzzle** are all toys.

Toys come in many kinds. Some toys we **build** with, like blocks. Some toys we **act** with, like dolls and toy cars. Some are **puzzles** we work out. And some we use to **make** things, like crayons and paper.

Toys are old. Children in ancient times made toys out of sticks, clay and cloth. Now toys are made in factories and sold in shops, but the reason is the same. Playing is how children learn about the world.

Every toy also needs a home. A toy box, a shelf or a basket keeps the floor clear and helps you find what you want next.
examples: This is my toy. I play with it every day.
I like building toys the best.
The toy box is under the bed.
sections.heading: What is a toy?

sections.body:
Building toys teach your hands and your brain to work together.

Blocks are small wooden or plastic pieces. You make a tower, a road, or a house. A good tower is wide at the bottom and narrow at the top. Then it does not fall over.

Puzzle pieces are flat shapes with a picture cut into them. When you fit the right piece into the right hole, the picture appears. A puzzle with many pieces takes a long time.

A **shape sorter** is a box with holes in it. You drop a shape into the hole that matches it. That toy teaches you the names of shapes.

Crayons, pencils and paper are toys for making. You draw a house, a dog or a map. You can also cut, fold and glue paper to make a paper hat.

Balls are simple and very useful. You throw them, catch them and kick them. A soft ball is safe to play with indoors.

Try one thing at a time and see what happens. Toys teach you best when you play slowly and watch carefully.
examples: I build a tower with the blocks.
This puzzle piece fits right here.
I draw a house with my crayons.
sections.heading: Toys we build and think with

sections.body:
Some toys are for pretending. When you play with them, you become someone else.

A **doll** can be a baby, a doctor or a cat. You talk for the doll and give it a name.

Toy cars, **buses** and **trains** make a road. A cardboard box with lines drawn on it is a garage. Then the cars have somewhere to go.

A **soft toy**, like a teddy bear or a rabbit, is for hugging. Small children often sleep with one. They are called **comfort toys** for that reason.

Action figures are toys that stand up and move. Some of them are heroes from stories. You act out the story with them.

And **puppets** are toys you hold and make talk. You put one on your hand, and you speak for it.

Pretending helps you learn. When you play the doctor, you learn how to be gentle and how to help. When you play the teacher, you learn how to listen.
examples: The bus is driving to the garage.
I put the puppet on my hand and talk.
sections.heading: Toys we act and tell stories with

sections.body:
These are the words for the toys you play with. Say them out loud and point to each toy as you find it.

A **block** is a small flat piece that you build with.

A **doll** is a small person toy that you talk for.

A **puzzle** is a game with many pieces that fit together.

A **ball** is a round toy you throw and catch.

A **teddy bear** is a soft toy with fur. You can hug it.

And a **toy box** is where the toys live when you are not playing.
examples: The doll sits on the chair.
Can I throw the ball outside?
sections.heading: The toy words, one by one

terms.example: I put the red block on top.
terms.gloss: A small flat piece of wood or plastic. You build towers and houses with blocks.
A small toy that looks like a person. You talk for it and give it a name.

terms.example: I finished the puzzle before dinner.
terms.gloss: A game with many pieces. You fit the pieces together to make a picture.
A round toy. You throw it, catch it and kick it.

terms.example: My teddy bear sleeps on my pillow.
terms.gloss: A soft toy with fur. Many children hug it or sleep with it.

sections.body:
Playing well is a skill, like tying your shoes. Here is an order that works every time.

First, choose one toy and clear a space. Put the others in the toy box.

Next, make a plan. You can say out loud, "Today I am going to build a tall tower." A plan makes play better.

Then play. Try one new thing. Try a big block on top, or a new road for the cars.

After a while, stop and look. Does the tower stand? Does the puzzle look right? This is the fun part.

Now it is time to tidy. Put each toy back in its own place. Wipe the table. Wash your hands.

If you play with friends, add two rules. Take turns, and say sorry when you bump someone. Those two rules make every game better.
examples: Today I am going to build a tall tower.
Can I have the next turn?
sections.heading: How to play a good game and tidy up
steps: Choose one toy and clear a space.
Say what you are going to build or play.
Play and try one new thing.
Stop and look at what you made.
Put every toy back and wash your hands.

sections.body:
Toys last longer when you treat them well.

Put them away. Toys on the floor get stepped on and broken.

Wash them now and then. Wipe a dirty toy with a damp cloth. Ask an adult before you wash a toy with water.

Keep small parts away from little brothers and sisters. Some toy pieces are too small to swallow.

Fix a broken toy. A little tape often saves a car. If you cannot fix it, ask an adult.

Grow your collection slowly. A few good toys that you really play with are better than a big heap that nobody touches.

And **give away or share the ones you never play with.** Another child will be happy to have them.
examples: I put my toys away before dinner.
I wipe the dirty car with a damp cloth.
I share my blocks with my friend.
sections.heading: Taking good care of your toys

item.summary: A toy is something we play with, and every toy has a way to play with it. After reading this, you can name the toys around you, choose the right game for each toy, play well with friends, and keep your toys in good shape.
item.title: Toys and How We Play With Them
